title: Prothrombin time (PT)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

sources.title: MedlinePlus: Prothrombin Time Test and INR (PT/INR)

measures: A prothrombin time (PT) test measures how many seconds it takes for a clot to form in a blood sample. Prothrombin is a protein made by the liver and is one of several clotting factors that work together to form a blood clot.
context: This test helps show if blood is clotting normally and can check whether a blood-thinning medicine is working. Alcohol, foods high in vitamin K such as green leafy vegetables, soybean and canola oils, high-fat diets, and some medicines and supplements can affect the result.
aboveRange: A longer clotting time may be associated with a bleeding disorder, in which blood does not clot well
A lack of vitamin K, which plays a role in blood clotting
belowRange: A shorter clotting time can be associated with a clotting disorder, in which the body forms too many clots
Supplements with vitamin K, or a diet high in vitamin K
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
